correctness.rationale: The critical dimension equation is correct. Direct coefficient reconstruction independently reproduced \(P_4=3297280\), \(P_5=420760566875\), \(P_7=279101475496912988004267637\), and the displayed huge \(P_8\). For even \(d\), a factor \(dx\) kills the product mod two. For odd \(d=2m+1\), parity of the composition factors gives \(Q_d\equiv(xyz)^A(x+y+z)^{3q}\), reducing the target coefficient to \(K_q\). Legendre valuation gives the first power-of-two contribution \(-1\), all later contributions nonnegative, and for every \(q\ge3\) at least one positive contribution; \(K_1=1,K_2=5\). Hence only \(d=5,7\) are odd. Complex conjugation then proves the stated real transverse corollary.

originality.rationale: Originality passes. The full accessible Hashimoto--Kadets article was inspected at its Fano numerology section: it restates the Debarre--Manivel coefficient formula and proves divisibility of a finite Fano degree by the defining degrees to the power \(r+1\). That explains evenness for even hypersurface degree but gives no parity information for odd degree. The nearby line-count parity result has \(r=1\) and a different critical equation. No checked source states that the critical plane count is odd exactly for degrees five and seven.
residual_risks: Classical enumerative tables may record some isolated plane counts or the hook-number parity separately; no source found combines them into the critical hypersurface iff theorem.
